root_cause.text: f2fs_fill_super() mishandled the positive return value from f2fs_recover_fsync_data() during read-only norecovery/disable_roll_forward mounts, propagating it as a successful positive status to vfs_get_tree() instead of converting or clearing it as an error condition.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the branch after `err = f2fs_recover_fsync_data(sbi, true);` to explicitly handle `err > 0` for read-only mounts by logging `"drop all fsynced data"` and setting `err = 0`, while the commit message states that the code "missed to handle error number returned from f2fs_recover_fsync_data() ... result in returning a positive error number to vfs_get_tree()" and shows `get_tree()` returned `1` before the BUG.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch changes the branch after `err = f2fs_recover_fsync_data(sbi, true);` to explicitly handle `err > 0` for read-only mounts by logging `"drop all fsynced data"` and setting `err = 0`, while the commit message states that the code "missed to handle error number returned from f2fs_recover_fsync_data() ... result in returning a positive error number to vfs_get_tree()" and shows `get_tree()` returned `1` before the BUG.

intent_record.intent_summary: Allow readonly mounts to succeed when fsync recovery is needed by dropping pending fsynced data instead of failing, while preserving the existing error path for writable mounts.
intent_record.what: The code after calling f2fs_recover_fsync_data(sbi, true) was changed from a single condition `if (!f2fs_readonly(sb) && err > 0)` that logged an error, set `err = -EINVAL`, and jumped to `free_meta`, into a nested `if (err > 0)` block that preserves the existing failure path for non-readonly mounts but adds a new readonly branch that logs `"drop all fsynced data"` with f2fs_info() and resets `err` to 0.
intent_record.how: At runtime, positive recovery results from f2fs_recover_fsync_data() are now handled differently for readonly mounts: instead of falling through without special handling, the mount explicitly accepts the situation, reports that fsynced data is being dropped, and continues successfully. For non-readonly mounts, the behavior remains to reject the mount with -EINVAL and require fsync data recovery.

grouping_result.intent: Allow readonly mounts to succeed when fsync recovery is needed by dropping pending fsynced data instead of failing, while preserving the existing error path for writable mounts.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly targets the mount-time handling of fsync recovery on read-only mounts, which is the same area as the root cause: incorrect treatment of f2fs_recover_fsync_data() results during read-only norecovery/roll-forward-disabled mounts.

candidates.rationale: This assigns the positive return from fsync recovery into err, and that value is later allowed to propagate on read-only mounts because only writable mounts with err > 0 are converted to an error.
This conditional only handles positive recovery return values for writable mounts, leaving the read-only case unhandled so a positive status can escape as a successful mount result.

vuln_statements.explanation: This stores the positive return value from f2fs_recover_fsync_data() into err. In the read-only norecovery/disable_roll_forward path, that positive status was not cleared or converted, allowing it to propagate upward as a successful positive mount result, which is the root cause.

This condition only treats positive err values as an error for writable mounts. By excluding read-only mounts, it leaves the positive recovery status unhandled in the affected path, permitting the incorrect positive return to escape to vfs_get_tree().

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant logic is visible in `f2fs_fill_super()`, so the snippet is sufficient. In the recovery path, the code does `err = f2fs_recover_fsync_data(sbi, true);` and then only converts a positive return to an error when the mount is not read-only: `if (!f2fs_readonly(sb) && err > 0) { err = -EINVAL; ... goto free_meta; }`. This means for read-only mounts, including the norecovery/disable_roll_forward case described in the root cause, a positive return from `f2fs_recover_fsync_data()` is left unchanged and can propagate out of `f2fs_fill_super()` as a positive success-like status. There is no handling here to clear or convert `err > 0` for the read-only recovery-disabled case. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present, and the fix is not yet present.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 6781eabba1bdb133eb9125c4acf6704ccbe4df02
Author: Jaegeuk Kim <jaegeuk@kernel.org>
Date:   Wed Mar 23 16:12:58 2016 -0700

    f2fs: give -EINVAL for norecovery and rw mount
    
    Once detecting something to recover, f2fs should stop mounting, given norecovery
    and rw mount options.
    
    Signed-off-by: Jaegeuk Kim <jaegeuk@kernel.org>

diff --git a/fs/f2fs/super.c b/fs/f2fs/super.c
index f5fbbfdb3d93..8f9648ffbbc3 100644
--- a/fs/f2fs/super.c
+++ b/fs/f2fs/super.c
@@ -1562,14 +15
bic_trace_step.reason: The diff is sufficient because it shows the exact handling around fsync recovery in f2fs_fill_super(). The vulnerable root cause was propagating a positive return from f2fs_recover_fsync_data() during norecovery/disable_roll_forward handling instead of converting it to an error. In this commit, the code distinguishes negative and positive returns: in the recovery path it now does `err = recover_fsync_data(sbi, false); if (err < 0) { ... goto free_kobj; }`, so positive values are no longer treated as generic success/error confusion there. More importantly, in the norecovery path it explicitly calls `err = recover_fsync_data(sbi, true);` and then checks `if (!f2fs_readonly(sb) && err > 0) { err = -EINVAL; ... goto free_kobj; }`. That is exactly the fix described by the root cause: a positive return indicating recoverable fsync data is converted into `-EINVAL` instead of being propagated upward as a positive success status. Therefore the vulnerable construct is not present in this commit version, and the fix is present.
